Reverse indexing recovers coordinates via $k = \lfloor \text{idx} / (N_x \cdot N_y) \rfloor$, $j = \lfloor (\text{idx} \pmod{N_x \cdot N_y}) / N_x \rfloor$, and $i = \text{idx} \pmod{N_x}$ [S1, unofficial].

The claim describes the mathematical inverse of the row-major indexing formula provided in Source [S1]. Source [S1] states the forward mapping is `idx = i + m_arraySize[0] * j + m_arraySize[0] * m_arraySize[1] * k`. Letting $N_x = m_arraySize[0]$ and $N_y = m_arraySize[1]$, the formula is $idx = i + N_x j + N_x N_y k$. Solving for $i, j, k$ yields: $i = idx - N_x N_y k - N_x j$. Since $0 <= i < N_x$, $i = idx mod N_x$. Then $(idx - i) / N_x = j + N_y k$. Since $0 <= j < N_y$, $j = ((idx - i) / N_x) mod N_y$, which is equivalent to $j = floor((idx mod (N_x N_y)) / N_x)$. Finally, $k = floor((idx - i - N_x j) / (N_x N_y))$, which simplifies to $k = floor(idx / (N_x N_y))$. Thus, the evidence supports the claim.
